text: Large language models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the most likely next word, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can get better results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at many tasks, including answering questions, summarising texts and translating languages. However, they also have limits. They sometimes produce false information, cannot check facts on their own, and may repeat biases found in their training data. For these reasons, it is always wise to review their output carefully.
